From 1d324c2f43f70c965f25c58cc3611c779adbe47e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Maoyi Xie <maoyixie.tju@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 18:33:18 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ip6_gre: Use cached t->net in ip6erspan_changelink().

After commit 5e72ce3e3980 ("net: ipv6: Use link netns in newlink() of
rtnl_link_ops"), ip6erspan_newlink() correctly resolves the per-netns
ip6gre hash via link_net. ip6erspan_changelink() was not converted in
that series and still uses dev_net(dev), which diverges from the
device's creation netns after IFLA_NET_NS_FD migration.

This re-inserts the tunnel into the wrong per-netns hash. The
original netns keeps a stale entry. When that netns is later
destroyed, ip6gre_exit_rtnl_net() walks the stale entry, producing a
slab-use-after-free reported by KASAN, followed by a kernel BUG at
net/core/dev.c (LIST_POISON1) in unregister_netdevice_many_notify().

Reachable from an unprivileged user namespace (unshare --user
--map-root-user --net).

ip6gre_changelink() earlier in the same file already uses the cached
t->net; only ip6erspan_changelink() has the wrong shape.

Fixes: 2d665034f239 ("net: ip6_gre: Fix ip6erspan hlen calculation")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v5.15+
Signed-off-by: Maoyi Xie <maoyi.xie@ntu.edu.sg>
Reviewed-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Kuniyuki Iwashima <kuniyu@google.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260430103318.3206018-1-maoyi.xie@ntu.edu.sg
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/ipv6/ip6_gre.c b/net/ipv6/ip6_gre.c
index 63fc8556b475..365b4059eb20 100644
--- a/net/ipv6/ip6_gre.c
+++ b/net/ipv6/ip6_gre.c
@@ -2262,10 +2262,11 @@ static int ip6erspan_changelink(struct net_device *dev, struct nlattr *tb[],
 				struct nlattr *data[],
 				struct netlink_ext_ack *extack)
 {
-	struct ip6gre_net *ign = net_generic(dev_net(dev), ip6gre_net_id);
+	struct ip6_tnl *t = netdev_priv(dev);
 	struct __ip6_tnl_parm p;
-	struct ip6_tnl *t;
+	struct ip6gre_net *ign;
 
+	ign = net_generic(t->net, ip6gre_net_id);
 	t = ip6gre_changelink_common(dev, tb, data, &p, extack);
 	if (IS_ERR(t))
 		return PTR_ERR(t);
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a bug in the `ip6erspan_changelink()` function in `net/ipv6/ip6_gre.c`. The change ensures that the per-netns hash table is correctly accessed by using the tunnel's cached `t->net` instead of `dev_net(dev)`, which may have changed after a network namespace migration.

#### Modifications per File:

- **File: `net/ipv6/ip6_gre.c`**
  - In `ip6erspan_changelink()`:
    - Moved the declaration of `t` (the tunnel structure) before the declaration of `ign` (the per-netns data).
    - Changed the initialization of `ign` from `net_generic(dev_net(dev), ip6gre_net_id)` to `net_generic(t->net, ip6gre_net_id)`, using the tunnel's cached `net` pointer instead of the device's current net.

#### Relationships Between Modifications:

- The reordering and initialization change are directly related: by declaring `t` first, the code can use `t->net` to correctly obtain the `ip6gre_net` structure for the netns where the tunnel was originally created. This aligns `ip6erspan_changelink()` with the existing behavior of `ip6gre_changelink()` (already using `t->net`), fixing a stale hash entry problem that led to a slab-use-after-free and kernel BUG when the original netns was destroyed after `IFLA_NET_NS_FD` migration.

ip6_gre: Use cached t->net in ip6erspan_changelink().

After commit 5e72ce3e3980 ("net: ipv6: Use link netns in newlink() of
rtnl_link_ops"), ip6erspan_newlink() correctly resolves the per-netns

This re-inserts the tunnel into the wrong per-netns hash. The
original netns keeps a stale entry. When that netns is later
destroyed, ip6gre_exit_rtnl_net() walks the stale entry, producing a
slab-use-after-free reported by KASAN, followed by a kernel BUG at

Reachable from an unprivileged user namespace (unshare --user

Fixes: 2d665034f239 ("net: ip6_gre: Fix ip6erspan hlen calculation")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v5.15+
Signed-off-by: Maoyi Xie <maoyi.xie@ntu.edu.sg>
Reviewed-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Kuniyuki Iwashima <kuniyu@google.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260430103318.3206018-1-maoyi.xie@ntu.edu.sg
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
Using dev_net(dev) instead of t->net in ip6erspan_changelink() leads to incorrect per-netns hash lookup after namespace migration, causing stale entries and use-after-free.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int ip6erspan_changelink(struct net_device *dev, struct nlattr *tb[],
 				struct nlattr *data[],
 				struct netlink_ext_ack *extack)
 {
-	struct ip6gre_net *ign = net_generic(dev_net(dev), ip6gre_net_id);
+	struct ip6_tnl *t = netdev_priv(dev);
 	struct __ip6_tnl_parm p;
-	struct ip6_tnl *t;
+	struct ip6gre_net *ign;
 
+	ign = net_generic(t->net, ip6gre_net_id);
 	t = ip6gre_changelink_common(dev, tb, data, &p, extack);
 	if (IS_ERR(t))
 		return PTR_ERR(t);
 
 	ip6erspan_set_version(data, &p);
 	ip6gre_tunnel_unlink_md(ign, t);
 	ip6gre_tunnel_unlink(ign, t);
 	ip6erspan_tnl_change(t, &p, !tb[IFLA_MTU]);
 	ip6erspan_tunnel_link_md(ign, t);
 	ip6gre_tunnel_link(ign, t);
 	return 0;
 }

This is precisely the root cause described: after namespace migration, `dev_net(dev)` retrieves the current namespace instead of the original link netns, causing incorrect per-netns hash operations and potential use-after-free. The fix requires using `t->net` obtained from the tunnel's private data. Since the snippet uses the buggy approach before `t` is even assigned, it contains the bug.
